reconcile.note: Henry reads Proverbs 22:15's rod of correction as effective only while character is still forming, so 27:22's entrenched fool has already outgrown that window.

discrepancy.emptyNote: R. N. Whybray catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: R. N. Whybray, The Composition of the Book of Proverbs (1994).

sides.snippet: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child: The rod of discipline drives it far from him.
sides.verseText: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child: The rod of discipline drives it far from him.

sides.snippet: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, Yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
sides.verseText: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, Yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
